questions.stem: ________ is the study of the origin, shape, size and classification of towns and cities.
explanation_steps: The textbook lists the fields of human geography: 'Urban Geography: the study of the origin, site, shape and classification of towns and cities.'

Population geography studies the number and distribution of people, economic geography studies economic activities, cultural geography studies culture, and political geography studies states and boundaries. Answer: D.
tips: Look for the key word: towns and cities → urban; people → population; production and trade → economic; states and boundaries → political.

similar_questions.stem: The branch of human geography that studies the distribution, density and growth of people is
explanation_steps: It is about the people themselves: their number, distribution and growth.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – The Subject Matter of Geography
textbook_ref.section: 1.2 Fields of modern geography – human geography

questions.stem: Colorado Desert is found in
explanation_steps: The textbook lists the hot deserts of the world, including the 'Mohave, Colorado and Mexican Deserts in Central and North America'.

It lies in the south-western USA (California) and north-western Mexico. Africa has the Sahara, Kalahari and Namib; Australia has the Great Australian Desert; South America has the Atacama; northeast India has the Thar. Answer: C.
tips: Hot deserts lie on the western sides of continents between about 15° and 30° latitude, where cold currents and trade winds keep the air dry.

similar_questions.stem: The Atacama Desert is found in
explanation_steps: The Atacama lies in northern Chile, on the west coast of South America.
Answer: D.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – Major Types of World Climates

questions.stem: One of the following African countries is located away from an area of active earthquake.
explanation_steps: Earthquakes happen mainly along plate boundaries. The textbook says tectonic forces produce 'rift valleys, block mountains, volcanoes, and earthquakes along the plate boundaries'.
Eritrea, Ethiopia, Djibouti and Kenya all lie on or beside the East African Rift System and the Afar triangle, where the African plate is splitting apart.
Niger lies in the stable interior of West Africa, far from any plate boundary. Answer: C.
tips: In Africa, active earthquake and volcanic zones follow the Great Rift Valley (Red Sea – Afar – Ethiopia – Kenya – Tanzania).

similar_questions.stem: Which African country lies on the Great Rift Valley?
explanation_steps: The Eastern (Gregory) Rift runs through the middle of Kenya.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The type of valley formed by glacial erosion is ____ valley.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'A U-shaped valley has a flat floor and steep sides. It is formed by the' erosion of a glacier moving down a former river valley.
A river cuts downward in its upper course and forms a V-shaped valley; a glacier fills the whole valley and scours both the floor and the sides into a U shape. Answer: A.
tips: River → V-shaped valley; glacier → U-shaped valley (a trough with hanging valleys at the sides).

similar_questions.stem: A narrow valley with steep sides formed by a river in its upper course is a
explanation_steps: Rapid vertical erosion by a river produces a V-shaped valley.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 8 – Map Work: Landforms on Contour Maps
textbook_ref.section: 8.2 Valleys on contour maps – V- and U-shaped valleys

questions.stem: An imaginary circle which is equidistant between north pole and south pole is called the
explanation_steps: The Equator (0° latitude) is the great circle lying exactly halfway between the North and South Poles; it divides the earth into the northern and southern hemispheres.
The tropics lie at 23½° N and S, so they are not equidistant from both poles. The Prime Meridian and the Date Line are half-circles joining the poles. Answer: A.
tips: Lines of latitude (parallels) run east–west; lines of longitude (meridians) run from pole to pole.

similar_questions.stem: The line of 0° longitude passing through Greenwich is the
explanation_steps: Longitudes are measured east and west from the Prime Meridian.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.section: 2.2 The shape of the earth – latitude and longitude

questions.stem: Eritrea is bounded by ________ to the north and west.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Eritrea is bounded on the east by the Red Sea, on the southeast by Djibouti, on the south by Ethiopia and on the north and west by the Sudan.'
South Sudan does not border Eritrea at all. Answer: B.
tips: Eritrea's neighbours: Sudan (north and west), Ethiopia (south), Djibouti (south-east), Red Sea (east).

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea's south-eastern neighbour is
explanation_steps: Djibouti borders Eritrea at the southern tip of the Southern Red Sea region.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 6 – Strategic Position, Size and Shape of Eritrea

questions.stem: Which of the following rivers is a perennial river in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The textbook calls the Setit (Tekeze) Eritrea's only 'perennial river': it flows all year because it rises in the high, rainy Ethiopian highlands.
The Mereb–Gash, Anseba and Barka are seasonal: they flow only during and shortly after the Kremti rains. Answer: D.
tips: Perennial = flows all year; seasonal (intermittent) = flows only in the rainy season. The Setit forms part of Eritrea's south-western border.

similar_questions.stem: The upper course of the River Gash is called the
explanation_steps: The Mereb becomes the Gash after it leaves the highlands.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Relief and Drainage Systems in Eritrea

questions.stem: A type of landform that has a flat top surface bounded by steep sides is a
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Plateaus are highlands with steep slopes and a broad and fairly flat top.'
Hills and mountains rise to peaks or rounded tops, plains are low and flat without steep sides, and a ridge is long and narrow. Answer: E.
tips: Plateau = 'table-land': high, flat-topped and with steep edges (escarpments). The Eritrean central highlands are a plateau.

similar_questions.stem: A large area of low, fairly level land is a
explanation_steps: Plains are low and flat; plateaus are high and flat.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Of the planets in the solar system, the nearest to the sun is
explanation_steps: The textbook's planet table gives Mercury the smallest distance from the sun (about 58 million km) and the shortest revolution (88 days).
Order from the sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Answer: A.
tips: Memory aid: 'My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles'.

similar_questions.stem: The largest planet in the solar system is
explanation_steps: Jupiter is the largest of the giant planets.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: An instrument used to measure air pressure is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The instrument used to measure air pressure is called a Barometer.' The mercury barometer and the aneroid barometer are the common kinds.
An anemometer measures wind speed, a thermometer temperature, a rain gauge rainfall and a wind vane wind direction. Answer: B.
tips: Air pressure is given in millibars; lines joining places of equal pressure are isobars.

similar_questions.stem: A barometer that works without liquid, using a sealed metal box, is the
explanation_steps: 'Aneroid' means 'without liquid'.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: In the future, water demand of Eritrea is expected to increase due to
explanation_steps: More people need more drinking and household water; expanding irrigated agriculture needs more water; new industries and mines need process water; and rising living standards increase domestic use.
All four are reasons, so the answer is E.
tips: When every option is a valid reason and 'All of the above' is offered, choose it.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a way of meeting Eritrea's growing water demand?

options.D: Leaving runoff to flow to the sea

explanation_steps: Dams store rainy-season runoff for use in the dry season.
Answer: A.

textbook_ref.section: 2.3 Water use and demand in Eritrea

questions.stem: The inorganic matter of soil is mainly derived from
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The inorganic components are the products of rocks and minerals that have been gradually broken down by weathering.'
Humus and the remains of plants and animals are the organic part of soil; air fills pore spaces but is not the source of mineral matter. Answer: B.
tips: Soil = mineral (inorganic) matter from weathered parent rock + organic matter (humus) + water + air.

similar_questions.stem: Decomposed plant and animal matter in the soil is called
explanation_steps: Humus is the dark organic part of the soil.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The cheapest form of transport is
explanation_steps: The Business & Economics textbook: 'For transporting heavy and bulky goods at the cheapest cost possible, Water Transportation is the best.'

Air is the most expensive; road and rail cost more per tonne-kilometre than ships. Pipelines are cheap too, but only for liquids and gases along fixed routes, so they are not a general form of transport. Answer: D.
tips: Air = fastest but dearest; sea = slowest but cheapest for bulky goods over long distances.

similar_questions.stem: The fastest but most expensive form of transport is
explanation_steps: Air transport is used for perishable or valuable goods because of its speed.
Answer: D.

questions.stem: Equinox is the time when the sun is directly over the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The equinox is the time when' the overhead sun is at the Equator (about 21 March and 23 September), so day and night are equal everywhere.
When the sun is overhead at a tropic it is a solstice (Cancer about 21 June, Capricorn about 22 December). The sun is never overhead at the poles. Answer: A.
tips: Equinox = 'equal night'. Solstice = the sun over a tropic, giving the longest or shortest day.

similar_questions.stem: On about 21 June the overhead sun is at the
explanation_steps: 21 June is the summer solstice of the northern hemisphere.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The most dominant type of vegetation cover in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: The Grade 12 textbook's land-cover table (Table 4.1) gives open and dense shrubland together as the largest vegetation class (about 22% of the country), ahead of woodland, grassland and forest.
On the same page the text also says acacia woodland 'occupies about a quarter of the surface', so woodland (C) can be defended from the wording. Forest and mangrove cover very small areas.
Key: A (shrub), with C also accepted.
tips: Eritrea is mostly arid and semi-arid, so shrubs and bushland cover more land than true forest.

similar_questions.stem: Mangrove vegetation in Eritrea is found mainly

options.B: along the Red Sea coast and islands

explanation_steps: Mangroves grow in salty tidal water along the coast.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Natural Vegetation and Wildlife in Eritrea

questions.review_flag: Two readings: Table 4.1 (G12 p47) makes shrubland (≈22%) the largest class, but the text on the same page says acacia woodland covers 'about a quarter' of Eritrea. Keyed A, C also accepted; teacher to decide.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, the <u>most</u> suitable region for growing coffee is the
explanation_steps: The textbook describes the central eastern escarpment (Merara, Fitche, Faghena, Filfil area) at about 1,700–2,400 m. It has mild temperatures and rain in both seasons, and it is where coffee and fruits are grown.
The lowlands and the Southern Red Sea are too hot and dry for coffee. Answer: C.
tips: Coffee needs mild temperatures, high humidity and rain in most months, which the green belt of the eastern escarpment provides.

similar_questions.stem: The Semenawi Bahri (Filfil) green belt lies on the
explanation_steps: It gets rain from both the summer and the winter wind systems.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Eritrea's economy is primarily based on
explanation_steps: The Grade 12 summary: 'Eritrea's economy is primarily based on agriculture.' Most of the people depend on crop farming and livestock rearing.
Mining is growing (Bisha, Zara, Asmara projects), but it employs far fewer people. Answer: C.
tips: Agriculture = crop production + livestock + forestry + fishing.

similar_questions.stem: Most Eritreans earn their living from
explanation_steps: About three-quarters of the population depend on farming and herding.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The Rashaida people of Eritrea occupy mainly the
explanation_steps: The textbook places the Rashaida, a Semitic-speaking pastoral people who came from Arabia in the 19th century, mainly along the northern Red Sea coast (Northern Red Sea region).
The Afar live mainly in the Southern Red Sea; the Kunama and Nara in Gash-Barka; the Bilen in Anseba. Answer: A.
tips: Link each ethnic group to its main region: Afar – Southern Red Sea; Rashaida – Northern Red Sea; Kunama, Nara – Gash-Barka; Bilen – Anseba.

similar_questions.stem: The Afar live mainly in the
explanation_steps: The Afar occupy the Danakil lowlands of the Southern Red Sea.
Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors influence the temperature of a place?
explanation_steps: Latitude controls the angle of the sun's rays; altitude lowers temperature by about 6.5 °C per 1,000 m; distance from the sea gives continental or maritime conditions; warm and cold currents warm or cool coasts.
All four influence temperature. Answer: E.
tips: Other factors include slope and aspect, cloud cover and the nature of the surface.

similar_questions.stem: Asmara is cooler than Massawa mainly because of
explanation_steps: Asmara is about 2,300 m higher than Massawa.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The <u>most</u> widely practiced type of agriculture in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: The textbook separates rain-fed and irrigated agriculture. Most Eritrean farmers are smallholders who depend on the Kremti rains, using ox-ploughs, to grow sorghum, barley, teff, millet and wheat.
Commercial, mechanised, plantation and export farming are limited to a few concessions and irrigated schemes. Answer: A.
tips: Subsistence rain-fed farming is typical of the highlands and western lowlands.

similar_questions.stem: Farming that uses water from rivers, dams or wells instead of rainfall is
explanation_steps: Irrigation brings water to the crops artificially.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Of the following countries in Africa, the one that borders the Mediterranean Sea is
explanation_steps: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt have coastlines on the Mediterranean Sea (the textbook's Mediterranean region includes North Africa).
Chad is landlocked, Kenya is on the Indian Ocean, Nigeria on the Atlantic (Gulf of Guinea), and Sudan on the Red Sea. Answer: D.
tips: Morocco borders both the Atlantic and the Mediterranean and faces Spain across the Strait of Gibraltar.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these African countries borders the Red Sea?
explanation_steps: Eritrea has about 1,200 km of Red Sea coast.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, the wildlife that is commonly found in Southern Red Sea region is
explanation_steps: The textbook says the African wild ass survives in the Danakil area of the Southern Red Sea (where 'the African wild ass is relatively in better condition'). It also lists the ostrich among the animals of the eastern and south-eastern lowlands.
Elephants are in Gash-Barka and lions are no longer found there. So both B and D are correct. Answer: E.
tips: When two single options are both right and a combined option exists, pick the combination.

similar_questions.stem: The endangered African wild ass in Eritrea lives mainly in the
explanation_steps: It is adapted to the hot, dry Danakil lowlands.
Answer: A.

questions.stem: ________ is made up of ice crystals formed near the ground when the temperature is below freezing point.
explanation_steps: When water vapour condenses on surfaces at temperatures above 0 °C it forms dew; below 0 °C it turns directly into ice crystals, which is frost.
Fog and mist are tiny water droplets suspended in air near the ground; clouds are droplets or ice high in the air. Answer: C.
tips: Dew point above freezing → dew; below freezing → frost.

similar_questions.stem: Water droplets that form on grass on a cool clear night (above 0 °C) are called
explanation_steps: Condensation above freezing gives dew.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The point where two rivers meet is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The point where two rivers or streams' join 'is called the confluence.'
A tributary is the smaller river that joins; a watershed divides two drainage basins; the mouth is where a river enters the sea or a lake; the source is where it begins. Answer: B.
tips: Khartoum stands at the confluence of the Blue and White Nile.

similar_questions.stem: A smaller stream that flows into a larger river is a
explanation_steps: Tributaries feed the main river.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 2 – Gradation by Rivers and Winds

questions.stem: During the summer season, the most dominant winds in Eritrea are the
explanation_steps: The Grade 12 textbook: 'During summer season, the dominant winds in Eritrea are the south-westerly winds.' They are the south-east trades deflected after crossing the equator, and they bring the Kremti rain.
The north-east trades dominate in winter. Answer: C.
tips: The summer south-westerlies are often called 'monsoon' winds in general books, but the textbook names them south-westerly winds, so choose C.

similar_questions.stem: In winter the dominant winds over Eritrea are the
explanation_steps: When the ITCZ moves south, the north-east trades blow across Eritrea.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, the distribution of elephants is limited to the
explanation_steps: The textbook reports 'elephants in the south-east Gash-Barka', along the Gash and Setit rivers where water and woodland are available.
The Red Sea regions are too dry, and the Semenawi Bahri forest has no remaining elephant herd. Answer: D.
tips: Eritrea's elephants move between the Gash-Setit area and neighbouring Ethiopia.

similar_questions.stem: Which wildlife is commonly associated with the Semenawi Bahri forest?
explanation_steps: The dense forest shelters forest mammals such as bushbuck, leopard and monkeys.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The <u>smallest</u> administrative region in Eritrea is Zoba
explanation_steps: The textbook's table of administrative regions gives Maekel (the Central region, around Asmara) only about 1,400 km², far smaller than the other five.
Maekel is the smallest in area, though it is the most densely populated. Answer: A.
tips: Largest regions: Northern Red Sea and Gash-Barka; smallest: Maekel.

similar_questions.stem: The capital of Zoba Debub is
explanation_steps: Mendefera is the administrative centre of the Southern region.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The source of all energy on earth is the
explanation_steps: The sun is the source of almost all energy on earth: sunlight heats the land and air, drives winds and the water cycle, and powers photosynthesis, which later gives fuelwood and fossil fuels.
The sun is not among options A–D (the moon, comets, galaxies and planets do not supply the earth's energy), so the correct choice is E, 'None of the above'.
tips: Read all options: when the obvious answer (the sun) is missing, 'None of the above' is correct.

similar_questions.stem: The energy the earth receives from the sun is called
explanation_steps: Insolation = incoming solar radiation.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 2.3 Insolation – distribution of the sun's energy

questions.stem: The type of climate where land is permanently covered with ice and snow is the
explanation_steps: The textbook groups the polar climates as the Tundra and the Ice Cap climates. In the ice cap climate (Antarctica, interior Greenland) no month rises above freezing, so the land stays permanently covered with ice and snow.
The tundra has a short summer when the snow melts and mosses and lichens grow. Answer: B.
tips: Tundra = warmest month 0–10 °C; ice cap = warmest month below 0 °C.

similar_questions.stem: Mosses and lichens growing during a short summer are typical of the
explanation_steps: The tundra thaws briefly in summer.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The second largest ethnic group in Eritrea is the
explanation_steps: The textbook's ethnic composition gives Tigrinya about 50% and Tigre about 31%, followed by much smaller groups (Saho, Kunama, Rashaida, Bilen, Afar, Nara and Hidareb).
So the Tigre are second. Answer: E.
tips: Eritrea has nine ethnic groups: Tigrinya, Tigre, Saho, Kunama, Rashaida, Bilen, Afar, Nara and Hidareb.

similar_questions.stem: The largest ethnic group in Eritrea is the
explanation_steps: The Tigrinya make up about half of the population.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The continent with the fastest population growth is
explanation_steps: Africa has the highest birth rates and a young population, so its natural growth rate (over 2.5% per year) is the highest of all continents.
Asia has the most people, but its growth rate is lower; Europe's population is almost static. Answer: A.
tips: Do not confuse the largest population (Asia) with the fastest growth (Africa).

similar_questions.stem: The continent with the largest population is
explanation_steps: Asia has about 60% of the world's people.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The majority of the population in the lowland of Eritrea is mainly engaged in
explanation_steps: The textbook: Eritrea has had a pastoral economy based in the lowlands and an agricultural economy based in the highlands. Lowland people are mainly pastoralists and agro-pastoralists keeping camels, goats, sheep and cattle.
Fishing is limited to the coast, and hunting and lumbering are minor. Answer: D.
tips: Low rainfall in the lowlands favours herding over crop farming.

similar_questions.stem: The mobile way of life of herders moving with their animals in search of pasture and water is
explanation_steps: Pastoral nomads move seasonally with their herds.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> in the category of developed countries?
explanation_steps: The textbook lists the developed countries (the USA, Canada, Western European countries such as Germany and Italy, Japan, Australia).
Argentina is a middle-income developing country of Latin America. Answer: D.
tips: Developed countries have high income per head, industrialised economies, high literacy and long life expectancy.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a developing country?
explanation_steps: Kenya is a low- to middle-income African country.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.section: 4.1 The concept of development – developed countries

questions.stem: The distance between the earth and the sun varies during different seasons of the year due to the

options.A: circular nature of the earth' orbit.
options.B: elliptical nature of the earth's orbit.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Because of the elliptical nature of the orbit, the distance between the earth and the' sun changes during the year: about 147 million km at perihelion (early January) and 152 million km at aphelion (early July).
A circular orbit would keep the distance constant. Answer: B.
tips: Perihelion = nearest (≈3 January); aphelion = farthest (≈4 July). Seasons are caused by the tilt of the axis, not by the distance.

similar_questions.stem: The position of the earth when it is farthest from the sun is called
explanation_steps: Aphelion occurs in early July.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which one of the following was <u>not</u> among the results of the Nilotic [Neolithic] revolution?

options.C: The development of division of labor
options.E: The emergence of inequality between men and women

explanation_steps: The paper prints 'Nilotic', but the options clearly describe the Neolithic (agricultural) revolution; 'Nilotic' is a misprint.

The textbook's 'Consequences of the Neolithic Revolution' lists permanent settlements (farming villages), food surpluses that 'encouraged the development of trade', specialisation and 'a division of labor', and a new relationship in which men gained more power than women.
Fire was already used by Paleolithic (Old Stone Age) hominids long before farming began, so it was not a result of the Neolithic revolution. Answer: D.
tips: Paleolithic: hunting and gathering, stone tools, use of fire. Neolithic: farming, domestication, villages, pottery, trade, division of labour.

similar_questions.stem: The Neolithic revolution refers mainly to the

options.B: beginning of agriculture and domestication of animals

explanation_steps: It was the change from food gathering to food production.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The Egyptian civilization was highly related to the
explanation_steps: Ancient Egypt grew along the Nile valley. The yearly flood left fertile silt, so the textbook asks students to explain why Egypt was called 'the gift of the Nile'.
The Indus supported the Harappan civilization, the Tigris and Euphrates Mesopotamia, and the Yellow River (Huang He) early China. Answer: E.
tips: River-valley civilizations: Nile – Egypt; Tigris–Euphrates – Mesopotamia; Indus – India; Huang He – China.

similar_questions.stem: Mesopotamian civilization developed between the
explanation_steps: Mesopotamia means 'land between the rivers'.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the following is mainly considered a City-State civilization.
explanation_steps: Ancient Greece is the classic city-state civilization: it was divided into independent poleis (Athens, Sparta, Corinth …), each with its own government, and it never formed one kingdom before Macedonian rule.

However, the textbook also describes 'The Sumerian City-states of Ancient Mesopotamia': 'These city-states were the basic units of Sumerian civilization.' So A can be defended too, although later Mesopotamia was ruled by empires (Akkad, Babylon, Assyria).
Egypt, China and India were united kingdoms or empires. Key: B, with A also accepted.
tips: Polis = Greek city-state (city + surrounding countryside, own laws and army).

similar_questions.stem: The two most famous Greek city-states were
explanation_steps: Athens (democracy) and Sparta (military oligarchy).
Answer: B.

additional_textbook_refs.unit: Unit 3 – Southwest Asia and Egypt (3500–500 B.C.E.)

questions.review_flag: Two defensible answers: Greece (classic polis civilization) and Mesopotamia (the textbook's 'Sumerian City-states', G9 p35). Keyed B, A also accepted; teacher to decide.

questions.stem: Identify the <u>correct</u> association.
explanation_steps: The textbook classifies the Eritrean languages into three groups: 'A) Nilotic language group: Nara and Kunama; B) Cushitic language group: Hidareb, Bilen, Saho and Afar; C) Semitic language group: Tigrinya, Tigre, and the Rashaida.'
Hidareb is Cushitic (not Nilotic), Kunama is Nilotic, Saho is Cushitic and Tigre is Semitic. Only Cushitic – Afar is right. Answer: C.
tips: Nilotic: Kunama, Nara. Cushitic: Afar, Saho, Bilen, Hidareb. Semitic: Tigrinya, Tigre, Rashaida (Arabic).

similar_questions.stem: Which Eritrean language belongs to the Semitic group?
explanation_steps: Tigrinya, Tigre and Arabic (Rashaida) are Semitic.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is <u>incorrect</u> about the Aksumite civilization?

options.B: It was highly dependent on maritime trade.
options.D: It was located in present day Eritrea and Northern Tigray.
options.E: It was founded by the Beja Kingdoms.

A change in the price of a single product (pizza, hamburgers or coffee) is a relative price change caused by that product's demand and supply. It does not by itself show a rise in the general price level. Answer: E.
tips: Inflation is measured with a price index (CPI) covering a basket of many goods, not one price.

questions.stem: Assume that the economy produces two goods, apples and butter, and that it is operating on its production possibilities curve. This economy can produce more apples if it

options.A: charges a lower price for apples.
options.C: charges a lower price for butter.

explanation_steps: On the PPC all resources are fully and efficiently employed, so unemployment cannot be reduced further (B is wrong) and prices do not change what can be produced (A, C are wrong).
The only way to get more apples is to move resources out of butter, that is, to produce less butter. This is the opportunity cost shown by the curve. Answer: E.
tips: Points on the PPC: efficient; inside: unemployment or inefficiency; outside: unattainable (unless the curve shifts out through growth).

People who dislike coffee, cannot afford it, or have tea or other substitutes available will demand little or none. All three reasons apply. Answer: D.
tips: Determinants of demand (other than own price): income, prices of substitutes and complements, tastes, expectations, number of consumers.

tips: In the long run all costs are variable; fixed costs exist only in the short run.

questions.stem: The opportunity cost of your attending college is the

options.A: cost of tuition, books and fees.
options.B: cost of room and board in the dorms if you live in campus.
options.C: wages you could have earned in a job if you were not attending college.

explanation_steps: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up. For a student, the big sacrifice is the income they could have earned by working instead.
Room and board is not part of it, because you must eat and live somewhere whether or not you attend college. So 'All of the above' (D) cannot be right.

In a full economic analysis tuition, books and fees are also part of the cost of going to college, but they are money (explicit) costs; the classic answer to this test item is the forgone wages. Answer: C.
tips: Opportunity cost = the best alternative forgone, not every money payment.

similar_questions.stem: Selam uses her free afternoon to study instead of working in a shop for 200 Nakfa or visiting friends. Her opportunity cost of studying is

options.B: the 200 Nakfa she could have earned (if that is her next best choice)

explanation_steps: It is the value of the best option given up.
Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Standard US test-bank item: keyed C (forgone wages). Tuition and books are also part of the economic cost of college (only room and board is excluded), so a teacher may see A+C as correct, but no option combines them.

options.B: total satisfaction gained by consuming the last unit of a good.
options.C: additional satisfaction gained by the consumption of one more unit of a good.
options.D: additional consumption divided by the additional satisfaction gained by the additional consumption.

explanation_steps: The textbook: the satisfaction from 'the consumption of one additional unit of a good is called marginal utility'.
A describes total utility, and D has the ratio upside down (MU = ΔTU ÷ ΔQ). Answer: C.
tips: Law of diminishing marginal utility: each extra unit gives less additional satisfaction than the one before.

Crude oil is a natural resource (land), a nurse is labour, a share of stock is financial capital (not a real resource), and a personal DVD is a consumer good. Answer: A.

questions.stem: If Michael stops going to the barber and has his wife cut his hair, then gross national product (GNP) will

options.C: remain the same but real GNP will increase.
options.D: remain the same but real GNP will decrease.
options.E: decrease but real GNP will increase.

explanation_steps: GNP counts only market transactions. The textbook lists 'non-market activities' among the items excluded from GNP.

The barber's paid service was counted; the wife's unpaid haircut is household production and is not counted. So measured GNP falls (and real GNP falls with it, since prices have not changed). Answer: B.
tips: Household work, do-it-yourself jobs and volunteer work are not in GNP; the same work bought on the market is.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is included in GNP?

options.A: A mother cooking for her family
options.B: The sale of a used car
options.C: A new house built and sold this year
options.E: Pocket money given to a child

explanation_steps: Only newly produced final goods and services sold on the market are counted.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Average propensity to save is the

options.A: fraction of any total income which is saved.
options.B: fraction of any total income which is consumed.
options.C: proportion of any change in income which is saved.
options.D: proportion of any change in income which is consumed.

explanation_steps: APS = total saving ÷ total (disposable) income, the fraction of total income that is saved. The textbook introduces the matching ratio for consumption, the average propensity to consume (APC = C ÷ Yd).
B is APC, C is MPS, D is MPC, and E is an identity, not a definition. Answer: A.
tips: Average = total ÷ total; marginal = change ÷ change. APC + APS = 1 and MPC + MPS = 1.

Medium of exchange = used to buy and sell; store of value = keeps purchasing power over time; standard of deferred payment = settles debts later. Answer: A.
tips: Four functions of money: medium of exchange, unit of account (measure of value), store of value, standard of deferred payments.

explanation_steps: The business (economic) entity concept says the business is treated as separate from its owner: the owner's personal assets, debts and spending are not recorded in the business's books.
Going concern assumes the business will continue; monetary unit means recording in money; periodicity divides life into periods; historical cost records assets at the price paid. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is used to record business transactions in date wise order?
explanation_steps: The general journal is the book of original entry. Transactions are journalised in chronological (date) order, with debits, credits and an explanation, before they are posted to the ledger accounts.
An account groups transactions by item (cash, sales …), not by date; a voucher is a single document; the balance sheet and trial balance are summaries. Answer: D.
tips: Order of the accounting cycle: source document → journal → ledger → trial balance → work sheet → financial statements → closing.
